🤖 **Assessment: not an automated-PR task (experiment launch, out of scope)**

**What this issue is.** A logbook/tracking stub for launching a production-priority v4-2048 run — the 2x long-context skew treatment twin of the qk=1.75 262K context-extension control, using the length-partitioned Datakit store from #8656 and preserving the checkpoint/optimizer/schedule/mesh/batch/data-offset from #6044. It is labeled `experiment`, not a bug report, and states no code defect.

**Why I am not opening a PR.**
- Launching a production-priority Iris run is governed by the `manage-hero-run` skill and requires explicit operator authorization plus live cluster submission. Per repo policy an agent does not submit production runs or bounce clusters without express permission. This is the opposite of a self-contained <100-line bug fix.
- There is no committed launcher to fix or extend: the qk=1.57 control and qk=1.75 runs referenced here exist only as W&B runs, and a repo search finds no `qk157`/`ctxext`/`262144` experiment module. So there is no code artifact this issue points at.

**To make this actionable as a repository change**, specify the concrete code deliverable and target path — e.g. "add a pinned launcher module at `experiments/.../ctxext_qk175_skew2x.py` that builds the treatment mixture (22.586% >64K / 77.414% ≤64K per #8656) from the length-partitioned store and the step-156k checkpoint." With that I can draft the launcher as a reviewable PR without submitting it. If instead you want the run actually launched, that needs an operator running the `manage-hero-run` workflow with an explicit go-ahead.

comments.body:
🤖 Degraded v4-2048 slice

The training child remains pending with all 256 tasks unstarted. The scheduler reports `need 256 workers in same tpu-name group, largest group has 254`.

The slice has 255 registered Iris workers. TPU host `t1v-n-25bf471b-w-74` has empty TPU metadata and registers as `worker-0`, colliding with the real `worker-0`. Controller logs show the same worker ID alternating between two IP addresses. The autoscaler therefore sees a degraded slice at its one-slice limit and cannot form the 256-worker gang.

No training step has run. Stopping and resubmitting only the job would retain this slice. Recovery requires replacing the degraded v4-2048 slice; no live mutation has been performed.

comments.body:
🤖 Recovery caveat

Six unrelated CPU tasks are bin-packed onto healthy workers in the degraded v4-2048 slice. Slice replacement would interrupt jobs owned by `dlwh`, `marin`, `michaelryan`, and `runner`.

The safe sequence is to preempt those six tasks so Iris reschedules them elsewhere, then force-delete the degraded queued resource and let the pending production job provision a fresh v4-2048 slice. No recovery action has been taken.
